**7B.5 Tinubu 2024 research note**
Overall read: **mixed, leaning negative**. Tinubu did make several technocratic appointments and some anti-rent-seeking moves, but the clearest concrete staffing signal is a family-linked appointment, and several relief/spending channels looked discretionary or opaque rather than cleanly professionalized.

| Assessment | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | President Tinubu establishes comprehensive economic coordination and planning system for Nigeria | State House | 2024-03-27 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-establishes-comprehensive-economic-coordination-and-planning-system-for-nigeria/ | Tinubu put the finance minister and CBN governor, plus economists and private-sector figures, at the center of emergency macro coordination. This is strong evidence for technocratic staffing rather than a patronage-only cabinet. | 7B.5; 7B.3 |
| Positive | President Tinubu appoints management team of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund | State House | 2024-04-05 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-appoints-management-team-of-the-nigerian-education-loan-fund/ | The presidency described the team as qualified Nigerians standing up a long-horizon social investment institution. This supports merit-based institutional staffing. | 7B.5 |
| Positive | President Tinubu appoints new Director General of the Bureau of Public Enterprises | State House | 2024-06-15 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-appoints-new-director-general-of-the-bureau-of-public-enterprises/ | The appointee was presented as a financial expert and chartered accountant, which is direct technocratic staffing evidence in an economically sensitive agency. | 7B.5 |
| Positive | President Tinubu directs reorganisation of the Bureau of Public Procurement | State House | 2024-06-15 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-directs-reorganisation-of-the-bureau-of-public-procurement/ | Tinubu ordered procurement reform to improve efficiency and transparency. That is the clearest anti-rent-seeking administrative move in the 2024 record. | 7B.5; 7B.4 |
| Positive | President Tinubu appoints new board of Family Homes Fund | State House | 2024-07-02 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-appoints-new-board-of-family-homes-fund/ | The board was framed as qualified Nigerians expected to use expertise to grow the real-estate sector. This is another merit-based staffing signal. | 7B.5 |
| Positive | Nigeria's Tinubu names seven ministers, sacks five in cabinet reshuffle | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-10-23 | https://theprint.in/world/nigerias-tinubu-names-seven-ministers-sacks-five-in-cabinet-reshuffle/2325625/ | Reuters described a standard reshuffle, while core portfolios like finance, defence, and planning were retained. That is weak counterevidence against a pure loyalist purge or patronage-maintenance reading. | 7B.5; 7B.3 |
| Negative | Tinubu under fire for appointing son-in-law head of housing agency | BusinessDay | 2024-02-21 | https://businessday.ng/news/article/tinubu-under-fire-for-appointing-son-in-law-head-of-housing-agency/ | This is the clearest family-interest conflict in the 2024 record. Tinubu appointed his son-in-law to head the Federal Housing Authority, which strongly cuts against clean separation from family advantage. | 7B.5; 7B.3; 7B.4 |
| Negative | Reps blame Agric ministry for delay in sharing Tinubu’s palliative | The Guardian Nigeria | 2024-01-09 | https://guardian.ng/news/reps-blame-agric-ministry-for-delay-in-sharing-tinubus-palliative/ | Rice palliatives were routed through lawmakers for constituent distribution, creating a discretionary and politically exposed channel. This is not proof of theft, but it is vulnerable to patronage-style allocation. | 7B.5; 7B.4 |
| Negative | Tinubu gives ministers 1,200 bags of rice each as palliatives for distribution | The Guardian Nigeria | 2024-09-16 | https://guardian.ng/news/tinubu-gives-ministers-1200-bags-of-rice-each-as-palliatives-for-distribution/ | Relief was also routed through ministers, again using politically mediated distribution instead of a clearly professionalized, arms-length delivery system. | 7B.5; 7B.4 |
| Negative | Tinubu, Shettima spend N8.64bn on travel expenses in three months | Punch | 2024-06-02 | https://punchng.com/tinubu-shettima-spend-n8-64bn-on-travel-expenses-in-three-months/ | This is evidence of heavy executive privilege spending. It does not prove personal enrichment, but it does show expensive office use and weak public discipline. | 7B.5; 7B.4 |
| Negative | FG spent N14.77bn on presidential jets in 11 months - State House report | Punch | 2024-06-23 | https://punchng.com/fg-spent-n14-77bn-on-presidential-jets-in-11-months-state-house-report/ | High-cost presidential fleet maintenance is negative evidence for clean, frugal office use. It is still indirect, but it raises opacity and privilege concerns. | 7B.5; 7B.4 |
| Negative | Nigeria has detained journalist who reported on corruption in widening crackdown | Reuters via GPB | 2024-05-09 | https://www.gpb.org/news/2024/05/09/nigeria-has-detained-journalist-who-reported-on-corruption-in-widening-crackdown | Detaining a corruption-reporting journalist under cybercrime law weakens scrutiny of elite behavior. That is indirect evidence that office-holders were not fully insulated from self-protective pressure. | 7B.5; 7B.4 |
| Negative | Nigeria police charge 4 journalists with cybercrimes for corruption reporting | CPJ | 2024-10-03 | https://cpj.org/2024/10/nigeria-police-charge-4-journalists-with-cybercrimes-for-corruption-reporting/ | Continued cybercrime charges against journalists show a punitive information environment late in 2024. That makes it harder to monitor whether appointments and spending were merit-based or patronage-driven. | 7B.5; 7B.4 |

**Search gap**
I did not find strong public 2024 evidence of direct bribes, hidden foundations, offshore assets, or explicit donor quid pro quo involving Tinubu or close family. The strongest evidence is indirect: one clear nepotistic appointment, discretionary relief channels, expensive executive spending, and pressure on corruption reporting.
